turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, that I will not hesitate to take action against any further oppression of my tenantry. You would do well to heed my words, lest you suffer the consequences.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, your tone suggests that you believe these threats are real, but what is it that you truly fear? Do you think the Mussulmans would attack without provocation?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: You and your fears, Nikhil, always an expert in the art of frightening oneself. I'm more concerned about your own estate's crops withering under your own incompetence.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I fear no fantasies, Sandip, but I fear the consequences of inaction in the face of clear and present danger.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Your words, Nikhil, are laced with a sense of urgency, but I sense a deeper concern, one that goes beyond mere property or power. What is it about your tenantry that you feel so strongly about?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, always so dramatic, I'm surprised you don't wear a cloak of doom to these meetings. As for my estate, I'll take my chances with the Mussulmans; at least they don't charge me interest on their sympathy.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be lectured by one who has so callously disregarded the well-being of his own tenants, Sandip.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, your concern for the tenantry is a curious thing. How do you propose we balance the needs of our people with the whims of those who live among us?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Pray tell, Nikhil, what's this newfound sense of compassion for the tenantry? Have you suddenly discovered a talent for empathy, or is it merely a clever ruse to further your own interests?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your flippant remarks, Sandip. Our people's safety is at stake, and I will not stand idly by while you gamble with their lives.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I sense a great deal of tension in this room, Nikhil. Might I ask, what specific actions do you propose we take to safeguard our people?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Bimala, my dear, I'm afraid Nikhil's apoplexy is simply a case of chronic martyrdom, and I'm his willing audience. He means well, I suppose, but his methods are as dull as his wit, don't you agree?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be mocked, Sandip. Our people's lives are not a jest to be used in your entertainment.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, your words suggest a deep concern for our people's well-being. Can you tell me more about the specific threats you've identified, and how we might work together to mitigate them?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Bimala, my love, Nikhil's theatrics are a wonder to behold, but I'm afraid his theatres are as empty as his arguments. I'll take his advice, but only if he's willing to join me for a spirited game of chess afterwards

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not engage in frivolous games with you, Sandip. The threat to our people's safety is no laughing matter.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, I've noticed that Nikhil's concerns seem to be rooted in a desire to protect our people, whereas your response has been dismissive. Can you tell me why you think his warnings are unnecessary?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Bimala, my dear, you know me well enough to know I'm not being dismissive, I'm just being realistic. Nikhil's warnings are as reliable as a stormy forecast from that old soothsayer, Mahesh.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, I must stress that your levity in the face of potential danger is a disservice to our people. The Mussulmans' intentions are not to be taken lightly, and I will not stand idly by while you downplay the threat.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, your concern for our people's safety is admirable, but I would like to know more about the specific incidents that have led you to believe the Mussulmans intend harm.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
